newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Historic Venezuela CANTV sell-off gets rolling.
newsitem.headline: Historic Venezuela CANTV sell-off gets rolling.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV began Tuesday its massive public share offering in both foreign and domestic markets, with local investors offered special terms in order to spread participation and dampen any latent nationalist sentiment.
"Now we'll really see how much faith there is in Venezuela, where the country's credibility stands," National Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto said in a television interview.

The sale, Venezuela's biggest ever and probably the largest in Latin America this year, has long been seen as a litmus test of the government's will to embrace tough structural economic reforms, analysts say.
But success is doubly crucial, they add, as it comes ahead of a slew of further privatisations in the iron, steel and banking sectors over the next few months.

While the government starts roadshowing in international financial centres, an estimated 200,000 Venezuelans will consider buying at preferential rates up to 50 million of the total 289 million shares offered.

Under the scheme, bids can range from 100,000 bolivars ($212) to five million ($10,600). Cash buyers will receive a three percent discount, while those that use the FIV's financing plan -- a two-year loan with 12 percent interest on a 30 percent downpayment -- will get a five-percent discount.
Once completed, the placement will nudge current Caracas bolsa market leader Electricidad de Caracas, which boasts some 60,000 shareholders, from its number one stock exchange spot.
However, CANTV shares bought on preferential terms have to be held for two years before they can be sold. That is to prevent an immediate fall in the price after the offering, Poletto said.
The final share price, due to be decided on November 21, is currently seen at between $3.07 to $3.50, Poletto added, although it could rise as soon as shares begin trading.
